measurement.source_call_unit: The six $61B5 updates are six qualifying $40CC fractional admissions, identified by the source-linked counter writes rather than inferred from six displayed frames. ROM $40CC reads selected rate $61C3; the $40ED-$40F7 fractional path adds $33 to $61B5 for rate $12 and carries into the step count. Disassembly has a startup/reset store at $0748 and the runtime $61B5 store at $40F3. Each labeled sample 1514-1519 shows exactly one $33 advance, no extra admission, and the source countdown advances once per sampled callback. Callback labels locate samples; they are not the movement unit.
measurement.movement_result: Six source-linked admissions add six base X steps plus one carry step, from X=$67 to $60: seven total pixels. Status $12, Y=$96, base/art=$18, attribute=$01 remain fixed.
measurement.same_route_b4_comparison: Retained natural-route B4 X values are $67,$66,$65,$64,$63,$62,$61 over callbacks1513-1519. The forced run matches through callback1518 and differs by the single expected carry pixel at callback1519 ($60 versus $61).
measurement.coarse_units_limit: This is six arcade $40CC admissions. It is not six CoCo logical ticks or six raw CoCo Vbords. Parent A11 evidence separately establishes an ordinary CoCo enemy pose phase over eight admitted simulation ticks with variable raw IRQ holds; movement-per-logical-tick remains a separate conversion question.

background_crosscheck.retained_b4_baseline: The B4 capture JSON reports the identical natural-route callback1517 change [[54908,6]] (54908 decimal = $D67C); callbacks1513-1516 and1518-1519 have no reported changes. Its raw D000-D7FF binary was not retained.
background_crosscheck.owner_evidence: At callbacks1513-1516 both B4 and A10 RAM snapshots have $6063/$6064 = $D67C, $6062=$FF, and $6061=$0F. At callback1517 both snapshots have $6063/$6064 = $D69C and $6061=$10. Current-ROM disassembly $39B8-$39C6 loads the border pointer at $6063, selects value $06 when $6062 is nonzero, and writes it through (HL); $39CC-$39CF computes/stores the next border pointer. The same exact state progression in the natural-route baseline proves this is the normal Part-1 border-color writer, not a rate-specific write.

official_device_map.mapping: $D400-$D7FF is 4-bit color RAM; $D000-$D7FF is handled by Lady Bug background read/write device.

background_crosscheck.differential_result: The sole changed byte and border-pointer progression exactly match B4 baseline; no intervention-attributable background difference was found. The color update occurs at callback1517 before the forced and baseline enemy X paths diverge at callback1519, so attributing it to the rate intervention is unsupported. This does not turn the original literal no-change predicate into a pass. The earlier A10 statement that B4 had no changes in this interval was incorrect and is corrected by this retained comparison.
